title: Does First-Token Shallow Alignment Extend to Open-Weight Audio Language Models?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with a gap: extending shallow alignment to audio is interesting but audio LLM deployments are less widespread than text, and the path to fixing the issue is the same as for text.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires working with audio-language models, text-to-speech conversion, and understanding audio model internals for prefilling. This is advanced for beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The audio processing pipeline (TTS + model inference + prefilling) adds significant engineering overhead beyond the core experiment. Sustained effort for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Audio-language model safety has been studied in terms of emotional variation vulnerabilities and jailbreak defense, but no published work tests whether the first-token shallow alignment phenomenon extends to audio modalities. The idea represents a novel modality extension of an established text-domain finding.

evidence.source: Investigating Safety Vulnerabilities of Large Audio-Language Models Under Speaker Emotional Variations (arXiv 2510.16893, 2025)
evidence.finding: Studies safety vulnerabilities in audio-language models under emotional variations but does not test for shallow alignment or first-token refusal patterns.

evidence.source: Defending Speech-Enabled LLMs Against Adversarial Jailbreak Threats (Interspeech 2025)
evidence.finding: Studies adversarial jailbreak threats on speech-enabled LLMs but focuses on defense mechanisms, not alignment depth measurement.

evidence.source: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep (Qi et al., ICLR 2025)
evidence.finding: Establishes shallow alignment in text models but does not extend analysis to audio-language models.
